findings.text: The legacy `command:<name>` event used to be emitted on the command itself (`this.emit`). It is now emitted only on `this.parent`. A listener registered on the command, e.g. `sub.on('command:sub', fn)`, silently stops firing after its action handler runs. A root command with an action handler has no parent, so it never emits at all. This is a backward-incompatible change in the event target.

The new `else if (this.parent && this.parent.listenerCount(commandEvent))` branch runs before the operands, `*` and `command:*` fallback. A command with no action handler whose parent listens for `command:<name>` now never reaches the unknown-command or help handling. For example, `prog sub extra` with `prog.on('command:sub', ...)` and no action on `sub` is swallowed instead of erroring on `extra`.

0.reason: The change moves the legacy command event emission from the command itself to its parent, which is a distinct backward-incompatible behavior change not related to the reference bug about unknown-option masking.

1.reason: The new parent-listener branch intercepts operands before the unknown-command/help fallback, causing extra arguments to be silently swallowed, which is a separate defect from the reference bug about unknown-option masking.
